turns.user: I signed as guarantor for my friend's bank loan. Under the Contract Act, 1872, how far does my liability as a surety extend compared to his?

gold.answer: Under section 128 of the Contract Act, 1872 the liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless the contract provides otherwise.

evidence.quote: The liability of the surety is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor, unless it is otherwise provided by the contract.

turns.user: Under the Arms Act, 1878, what is the maximum punishment for breaking a condition of an arms licence, when the act is not punishable under section 19 or section 20?

gold.answer: Section 21 of the Arms Act, 1878 (breach of licence) provides imprisonment up to six months, or a fine up to five hundred rupees, or both.

evidence.quote: be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both

turns.user: In Taj Muhammad v. The State (Criminal Appeal 234/2016), decided by the Sindh High Court, Circuit at Hyderabad on 23 December 2016, how much Daman was the appellant required to deposit before he was released after the compromise?

gold.answer: Rs. 25,000 as Daman. The offences were compounded under section 345 Cr.P.C. after the complainant forgave the appellant; the Daman was to be deposited with the Additional Registrar and the appellant was ordered to be released.

turns.user: In Khalid Ali v. Mst Amnat (II.A. 10/2008), decided by the Sindh High Court, Circuit at Hyderabad on 24 November 2017, did the court set aside the concurrent findings of the lower courts, and why or why not?

gold.answer: No. The second appeals were dismissed with no order as to costs, because at the stage of second appeal it is not open to re-appraise the evidence and the two concurrent findings were not in direct conflict with the record.

evidence.quote: at the stage of second appeal it is not open to re-appraise of the evidence
The appeals as such, are dismissed however, in the circumstances with no orders as to costs.

turns.user: My cousin is only 16 years old. Last month he signed a written agreement to sell me his motorcycle.
I already paid him 40,000 rupees as advance.
Now his father says the deal is off and he will not hand over the motorcycle.
Our families are not on speaking terms since then.
Considering the detail about him I gave you in my first message, which section of the Contract Act, 1872 decides whether he could make this agreement at all?

gold.answer: Section 11 of the Contract Act, 1872: only a person who is of the age of majority, of sound mind and not disqualified by law is competent to contract. A 16-year-old has not reached majority, so he was not competent to contract.

evidence.quote: Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject

turns.user: The trial court dismissed my civil suit for recovery of money as time-barred, even though the defendant never raised limitation as a defence.
I filed the suit in Hyderabad in 2023.
My lawyer says he was ill for several months before filing.
I still have the bank receipts for the original loan.
Based on what I told you at the start, was the court right to do that even though nobody objected? Which section supports your answer?

gold.answer: Yes. Under section 3 of the Limitation Act, 1908, every suit instituted after the prescribed period of limitation shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence (subject to sections 4 to 25).

evidence.quote: every suit institute, appeal preferred, and application made, after the period of limitation prescribed therefore by the first schedule shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence

turns.user: I am writing an assignment on section 460 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, about persons jointly concerned in house-breaking by night.
My teacher wants the answer in simple language.
The submission is due on Friday.
Please also include the exact citation.
Has this section been amended? Which law made the change, and in which year?

gold.answer: Yes. The amendment note for section 460 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 reads: Subs. by Act II of 1997, ss. 8 & 9. So it was substituted by Act II of 1997.

evidence.quote: Subs. by Act II of 1997, ss. 8 & 9.

gold.answer: Yes. The amendment note for section 54 of the Contract Act, 1872 reads: Subs. by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981 (XXVII of 1981), s. 3 and 2nd Sch.
